key_insight: Learned diffusion proposals help continuous constraint solving only in a narrow regime; for many problems, simple random multi-start with the same refinement budget is just as good or better.
engineering_relevance: For solver design, the biggest gains come from improving discrete structural choices and using exact polishing/checking, while learned value proposals should be adopted selectively based on problem regime.
method: Candidate-conditioned repair ranker selects among K structural augmentations for a constraint system.
MARC converts the system into a factor graph, uses a graph-neural diffusion denoiser to propose assignments, then refines them with exact algebraic descent and symbolic checking.
A controlled random multi-start baseline is evaluated under the same polish/check budget to isolate the true benefit of learned proposals.
evidence_signal: The repair ranker reached near-exhaustive performance with 0.997 balanced nonlinear menu accuracy versus 0.236 for random, and random multi-start followed by exact polish matched or exceeded learned proposals except in high-dimensional, weakly coupled cases.
watch_item: Reported gains may not transfer to real deployments unless the problem lies in the learning-favorable regime; otherwise, random restarts can eliminate most of the apparent advantage.
paper_title: When Do Learned Diffusion Proposals Help Constraint Solving? A Controlled Study on Continuous Algebraic Systems
